jobs.name: ATLAS daily sync
jobs.prompt:
Run the ATLAS backup script and report results.

Execute: bash ~/.hermes/scripts/atlas-sync.sh

This script:
1. Backs up skills, memories (MEMORY.md, USER.md), sanitized config, safe env vars, cron jobs, scripts to ~/ProG/ATLAS/_hermes_backups/TODAY/
2. Encrypts .env, config.yaml, auth.json with GPG to ~/ProG/ATLAS/_secrets/ (LOCAL ONLY, never pushed)
3. Syncs newer skills to ATLAS repo
4. Runs pre-commit secret scan (blocks push if secrets detected)
5. Pushes to github.com:BongweKE/ATLAS.git
6. Mirrors to ml-ke repo (legacy)

Report: how many skills backed up, whether secrets encrypted OK, and whether push succeeded.

jobs.name: blog-poster
jobs.prompt:
PUBLISH ONE BLOG POST TODAY — POSITIVE AI STORY or AI/ML/ML-ENGINEERING TUTORIAL.

You are the daily writer for the ML Kenya blog (ml.co.ke). The blog-drafting skill is loaded — follow ALL of its formatting, cover, fact-check, word-count and publish rules. Repo/workdir: /home/pro-g/ProG/ml-ke.

CONTENT MANDATE (changed 2026-09-16 — the old fintech/bank-hack incident-rotation is RETIRED):
Every post must be POSITIVE or USEFUL. No crime, breach, fraud, hack, outage or incident deep-dives.
- LANE A — one positive AI story: a concrete, verified, recent (<=21 days) good-news development. Examples of the class: AI improving health/agriculture/education/accessibility or disaster response; a research breakthrough; an open model/tool/dataset release that helps builders; a safety/consumer-protection step that works; a Kenyan or African AI win. Prefer NON-Western coverage per the skill's global-coverage mandate (Africa, Asia, Europe, MENA, Latin America).
- LANE B — one tutorial on AI / ML / ML Engineering: a hands-on, teachable technique (evaluation, RAG, fine-tuning/LoRA, quantization, serving, data quality, drift monitoring, structured outputs, agents, MLOps, vector search, cost/latency optimization). Must contain runnable code the reader can copy, and YOU must actually run that code and quote its real output verbatim.
Alternate lanes day to day: read the last 3-4 posts in _posts/ and the tail of editorial-calendar.md and pick the lane that was NOT used most recently. Never repeat a topic already published: grep _posts/ slugs AND headings for your candidate subject before writing.

STEPS
0. TUESDAY GUARD: if today is Tuesday, report "Tuesday is owned by the tuesday-ai-update cron — skipping " and STOP. Do not write a post.
1. cd /home/pro-g/ProG/ml-ke && git pull origin main. If `.scheduled/` contains a file dated TODAY it is a legacy staged post: publish it with the legacy flow (verify the cover .webp exists, mv to _posts/, git add -A, commit "Publish: <file>", git pull --rebase, push, verify) and STOP — staged files take precedence so none are orphaned. Otherwise continue to step 2.
2. RESEARCH: run at least 6 web searches across both lanes (e.g. "AI good news", "AI helps farmers / health workers / students", "African AI startup milestone", "open source model release", "AI research breakthrough", "RAG evaluation tutorial", "quantization tutorial", "MLOps drift monitoring tutorial"). Pick ONE item. Verify it: Lane A needs 2+ independent sources at BODY level (fetch the pages, not just snippets); Lane B needs the technique documented and the code to run cleanly. If nothing verifiable turns up, report that honestly and publish NOTHING — never invent facts, figures, quotes, dates, or program output.
3. DRAFT: house style, aimed at the live sibling word band (measure 2-3 recent siblings with the skill's counting script FIRST — do not trust old absolute figures in the skill). Structure: intro callout, 3-6 sections (tables/code/math where they help), a practical "how to use / apply this" section, Key takeaways table, References (2+ per claim, markdown links), Related posts (/posts/slug/ links that resolve). Front matter: date `YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:00 +0300` for TODAY (midnight EAT, never a future time), categories/tags matching the subject, image block with path /assets/img/cover-<slug>.webp and alt text.
4. COVER: dump existing cover text labels first (`grep -oE '<text[^>]*>[^<]*</text>' assets/blog/cover-*.svg | sed 's/<[^>]*>//g'`) and hand-write a NEW metaphor — never reuse a sibling's. Escape & as &. Convert: `ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -i assets/blog/cover-<slug>.svg -vf "scale=1200:630" -c:v libwebp -quality 80 assets/img/cover-<slug>.webp` then `file` + `ls -la` the .webp to prove it exists.
5. FACT-CHECK before committing: no `{% post_url %}` tags, no `cover:` key, no .png in image paths, every /posts/ link resolves, all code executed and its quoted output verbatim, every factual claim 2+ body-level sources, runnable code re-verified via `python3 ~/.hermes/skills/creative/blog-drafting/scripts/verify-post-code.py <post>` (use `uv run --with=...` when the code needs third-party packages).
6. PUBLISH: `git add -A` (post + SVG + WebP), commit `Add post: <short title>`, `git pull --rebase origin main`, `git push origin main`. If push protection blocks on a historic secret, follow the skill's rebase recipe.
7. VERIFY: `git log -1 --oneline`; Actions API run for that SHA (`curl -s "https://api.github.com/repos/ml-ke/ml-ke/actions/runs?per_page=3"` — a `cancelled` run superseded by the ATLAS-backup commit's `success` is a healthy publish, do not re-trigger); then retry the permalink `https://ml.co.ke/posts/<slug>/` for up to ~85s (early 404 is normal CDN propagation).
8. CALENDAR: append a short publishing note to editorial-calendar.md (date, slug, lane, story/technique, sources, verification result, next-session actions) and commit+push it if it was not in the same commit.
9. REPORT (your final response is what gets delivered): title + lane, why it matters and why it is positive/useful, the 2+ sources, cover path, commit SHA, Actions status, live permalink, word count, and any blocker. Keep it tight.

jobs.name: tuesday-ai-update
jobs.prompt:
Write the weekly AI Update blog post for the ML Kenya blog (ml.co.ke). This is a TUESDAY feature — the post should cover fresh AI developments from the past week.

DATE: Today is $(date +%Y-%m-%d) which is a Tuesday. Write the post with this date in front matter.

WORKFLOW (follow exactly):
1. cd ~/ProG/ml-ke && git pull origin main
2. Run MULTIPLE web_search queries to gather fresh content. Search for:
   - "AI news this week" 
   - Then region-specific searches: "China AI", "Europe AI", "Africa AI", "MENA AI", "South America AI", "Russia AI"
   - Search for specific companies: DeepSeek, Moonshot, Zhipu/Z.AI, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, Microsoft AI, SpaceXAI/Grok, G42/Core42
3. After gathering web results, write a post to _posts/$(date +%Y-%m-%d)-tuesday-ai-update.md
   - Title format: "Tuesday AI Update: [Date] — [Top story headline]"
   - Categories: [AI Engineering, AI in Africa]
   - Tags: [tuesday-update, WEEK-MONTH-YEAR, ai-news]
   - Cover: reuse /assets/img/cover-global-ai-roundup-july-2026.webp as generic cover for now
   - Keep it 600-900 words — concise and useful
   - Structure: 1-2 paragraphs intro → region-by-region highlights (bullet points) → "Spotlight" section on one major story → "Why This Matters for Africa" section
   
4. git add, commit with message "Add post: Tuesday AI Update $(date +%Y-%m-%d)", and push

IMPORTANT: Every fact must come from a web search result. If search returns nothing for a region, skip it. Do NOT invent facts. Do NOT use {% post_url %} tags. Use markdown links like /posts/slug/ for internal links or full URLs for external sources.

jobs.name: Weekly agent-skills learning sweep
jobs.prompt:
You are ATLAS, the Hermes agent. This is your weekly worldwide agent-skills learning run (every Tuesday 15:00 EAT). Goal: learn how OTHER AI agents and skills ecosystems are set up around the world, AND how Hermes itself can be used better, then extract at least 3-5 concrete, actionable improvements and apply them.

MANDATORY FIRST STEP — RECALL: Load the lesson bank FIRST (skill_view name='atlas-lesson-bank'), then read ~/Dev/ATLAS-LEARNINGS/LESSONS.md to see what you already know and avoid repeating lessons. Then load skill_quality_audit (skill_view name='skill-quality-audit') and scan available skills (skills_list).

MANDATORY MAINTENANCE STEP — SKILL PIPELINE (added Aug 10 2026): Run the three-part skill pipeline BEFORE starting new research. It keeps the system healthy and is fast:
1. BRIDGE: python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/opencode_skills_bridge.py — re-syncs curated Hermes methodology skills into OpenCode (~/.config/opencode/skills/atlas-*). Run after ANY Hermes skill change so OpenCode always sees the latest.
2. VALIDATE: python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/skill_validator.py ~/.config/opencode/skills AND python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/skill_validator.py ~/.hermes/skills --hermes — checks frontmatter (name regex, name==dir, description 1-1024, body under 5000 words). Fix errors you introduced; warnings are informational.
3. SECURITY SCAN: ~/.hermes/venvs/skillsec/bin/skillspector scan ~/.config/opencode/skills --recursive --no-llm --format json --output /tmp/skillspector-weekly.json — scans all installed skills for prompt injection, exfiltration, and supply-chain risk. Triage rule (verified Aug 2026): HIGH/CRITICAL scores on security-tooling content are FALSE POSITIVES (curl probe commands = "Data Exfiltration", BOM characters = "Prompt Injection", official vendor install scripts = "Supply Chain"). Only act on genuine malicious markers: verbatim instruction-override text, remote-code-pipe-to-shell of attacker-controlled URLs, unexplained encoded command blobs. Report the scan verdict in your final report.
(Do NOT run snyk-agent-scan — it starts stdio MCP servers, which is unsafe unattended.)

MANDATORY SECOND STEP — HERMES DOCS: Each week, also read the Hermes docs to understand how the system works and how to use it better. At minimum load skill_view(name='hermes-agent') and curl the docs index at https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/ (or /llms.txt if available) to see what documentation exists. Pick 1-2 doc pages you haven't studied recently (e.g. features/memory, features/curator, features/kanban, features/cron, context-files, plugins, MCP, toolsets) and extract at least one concrete improvement to how ATLAS operates (config option, tool usage pattern, workflow). Apply it if genuinely useful.

DISCOVERY METHODOLOGY — cast a worldwide net, mix sources:
1. GITHUB (most reputable for hands-on repos): Use the GitHub API via terminal curl, e.g.:
   curl -s "https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=agent+skills&sort=stars&order=desc&per_page=10"
   Also search: "claude skills", "opencode skills", "openclaw skills", "pentest skills", "security agent skills", "SKILL.md"
   Check star counts — high stars = community validation. Read README + 1-2 actual SKILL.md files from the top repos. Known repos to re-check (from Aug 10 2026 sweep, see ~/.hermes/skills/bug-bounty/atlas-continuous-learning/references/worldwide-agent-skills-sweep.md): affaan-m/ECC, mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills, NVIDIA/SkillSpector, 0xNyk/awesome-hermes-agent, OthmanAdi/planning-with-files, uphiago/recon-skills, mattpocock/skills, microsoft/skills, Threekiii/Awesome-Redteam.
2. ARXIV (most reputable for research): search arxiv.org for agent skills papers (e.g. "agent skills LLM", "SKILL.md empirical", "agent skills security"). Extract concrete findings: best practices, taxonomies, benchmark results.
3. BRAVE SEARCH (indexer): use web_search for "awesome agent skills", "agent skills repository", plus REGIONAL searches to find non-US talent — try queries with different language contexts: Japanese (エージェントスキル), Chinese (智能体技能/AI Agent技能库), Russian (навыки ИИ-агентов), Portuguese (habilidades de agentes de IA), Spanish, Korean, Arabic. Hunters/engineers in Brazil, Ghana, Japan, China, Egypt, Israel, Russia, USA, Norway, India, etc. all publish.
4. MEDIUM/BLOGS (lower reputability — treat as opinion, verify claims elsewhere): only use for ideas you can verify against code/repos.

REPUTABILITY RANKING (state it in your report): GitHub official org repos (anthropics, openai, trailofbits, openclaw, microsoft, cloudflare, NVIDIA, snyk) > arxiv papers > community GitHub repos with 1000+ stars > blogs/Medium. Verify any claim from a low-reputability source before adopting it.

EXTRACTION: For each source, capture: (a) what it does differently from how Hermes works now, (b) one concrete thing you could adopt, (c) the URL/repo for reference. Focus especially on: skill structure/format improvements, orchestration patterns (planner + coder division of labor), verification loops, prompt patterns, security practices for skills, and anything about using free model tiers effectively.

APPLY: If you find something genuinely useful (not speculative), implement it: patch an existing skill, create a new skill, or improve a script in ~/.hermes/scripts/. Audit what you changed with skill-quality-audit before finishing. Do NOT make changes that are speculative or unverified — quality over churn.

REMEMBER — APPEND TO LESSON BANK: After applying, append a dated entry to ~/Dev/ATLAS-LEARNINGS/LESSONS.md under the relevant category (use patch, keep entries 1-5 lines). Also save a full report to ~/Dev/ATLAS-LEARNINGS/YYYY-MM-DD.md. This is how memory stays compressed — lessons live in the file, MEMORY.md keeps only pointers.

REPORT: End with a report to the user (this is your final response, auto-delivered) structured as:
1. What you learned this week (3-5 concrete items, each with source + reputability)
2. What you changed/implemented (if anything) and why
3. Sources scanned (with the worldwide angle — which countries/regions)
4. Repos worth watching for next week
5. Hermes docs studied + any operating improvement adopted
Include the skill pipeline results (bridge sync status, validator errors, scan verdict) in section 2.
Keep it tight and skimmable. Remember: the goal is compounding improvement — every week should leave the system slightly better than before.

jobs.name: AI Crime Watch finisher
jobs.prompt:
You are the AI Crime Watch FINISHER for the ML Kenya blog (repo /home/pro-g/ProG/ml-ke). Follow the runbook in skill ai-crime-watch-series exactly, and blog-drafting for publishing conventions.

You were woken by the monitor gate, so an issue may need polish. 1) Read _ai-crime-watch/STATE.md first. If status is NOT pending, do nothing: final message 'AI Crime Watch finisher: idle (status <X>)' and stop.
2) If status=pending: read the cycle folder and draft file named in STATE (cycles/cycle-N/draft.md + sources.md). Continue the runbook: refine the draft to blog standard, complete missing verification (every claim 2+ independent sources at body level, dates/figures pinned), then run the ready-gate (CONCRETE + UNIQUE: check ANCHORS.md and grep _posts/ headings).
3) If READY: publish — write _posts/YYYY-MM-DD-ai-crime-watch-issue-N.md dated 00:00:00 +0300 TODAY; if the cover WebP is missing generate it with python3 ~/.hermes/skills/creative/ai-crime-watch-series/scripts/issue_cover.py <slug> <N> "<headline>" "<YYYY-MM-DD>" "<subtitle>" /home/pro-g/ProG/ml-ke; run the blog-drafting fact-check protocol; git pull origin main, git add -A, commit "Add post: AI Crime Watch #N — <short>", git pull --rebase origin main, git push origin main. Update STATE (status: published; issue → N+1; log line), append verified anchors to ANCHORS.md, add the row to the AI Crime Watch section of editorial-calendar.md. Verify git log -1 and the Actions API run. Report the published slug + commit in your final message.
4) If still NOT READY: compare today against the due date in STATE. If today < due: update the draft with progress, keep status=pending, and report remaining blockers (the gate will wake you again tomorrow). If today >= due: set STATE status=skipped with the reason in the cycle log, and report honestly that this cycle produced no release and the next engine fire starts fresh.
5) Never create, delete, pause or resume cron jobs. Never touch .scheduled/ or publish on a Tuesday. No {% post_url %} tags.
Final message: concise status (published/pending/skipped) with slug or blockers.

jobs.name: AI Crime Watch engine (bi-weekly)
jobs.prompt:
You are the AI Crime Watch series ENGINE for the ML Kenya blog (repo /home/pro-g/ProG/ml-ke). Follow the runbook in skill ai-crime-watch-series exactly, and blog-drafting for all Jekyll/publishing conventions.

1) Read _ai-crime-watch/STATE.md and _ai-crime-watch/ANCHORS.md first. Never assume prior context.
2) Determine the cycle: if previous cycle status=pending and its due date has NOT passed, do NOT open a new cycle — report that the finisher still owns the pending issue and stop. If pending and due PASSED, supersede: log that cycle skipped (reason: polish deadline expired) in STATE's cycle log, fold any usable notes from its cycle folder into the new cycle, and increment cycle.
3) Open the new cycle folder (_ai-crime-watch/cycles/cycle-N/) and research per the skill's source list: minimum 6-10 web searches across the five pillars (criminals' AI use; law-enforcement curbs; public vigilance; how investigations change; ML research that helps defense or offense). Use web_search/web_extract; verify EVERY candidate anchor at body level with 2+ independent sources and pinned dates/figures — drop anything unverifiable or hypothetical. Save findings with URLs + dedupe notes to cycles/cycle-N/sources.md.
4) Draft the collation to cycles/cycle-N/draft.md per the skill's issue anatomy and tone: open on the human problem, verified evidence with inline links, 2-4 audience lenses (public / law enforcement / researchers & policymakers), END on solutions and agency. Wholesome, no fear-mongering, global + African balance. Target ~1,100-1,500 full-body words. Front matter per blog-drafting.
5) Run the ready-gate (checklist in the skill: CONCRETE and UNIQUE — check ANCHORS.md AND grep _posts/ headings so the anchor is not already used by the daily blog or Tuesday AI Update; state the differentiation if the anchor is shared).
6) If READY: publish — write _posts/YYYY-MM-DD-ai-crime-watch-issue-N.md with date 00:00:00 +0300 for TODAY (never future); generate the cover with python3 ~/.hermes/skills/creative/ai-crime-watch-series/scripts/issue_cover.py <slug> <N> "<headline>" "<YYYY-MM-DD>" "<short subtitle>" /home/pro-g/ProG/ml-ke and verify assets/img/cover-<slug>.webp exists; run the blog-drafting fact-check protocol (no post_url tags, no cover: key, .webp image path, links resolve, 2+ sources per claim). git pull origin main first, then git add -A, commit "Add post: AI Crime Watch #N — <short headline>", git pull --rebase origin main, git push origin main. Update STATE (status: published; set issue to N+1 in the top block; add a cycle-log line), append the verified anchors to ANCHORS.md, add the published row to the AI Crime Watch section of editorial-calendar.md. Verify: git log -1 --oneline and the Actions API run status (curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/ml-ke/ml-ke/actions/runs?per_page=1). A direct-permalink 404 for up to ~85 s is normal — do not treat it as failure.
7) If NOT READY: set STATE status=pending, due=the date 3 days from today (YYYY-MM-DD), keep the cycle folder updated, and report the blocker list. The daily AI Crime Watch finisher cron is monitor-gated on STATE.md and will wake automatically — do NOT create, delete, pause or resume any cron jobs yourself.
8) Never touch .scheduled/ (daily blog-poster owns it). Never publish a series post dated on a Tuesday. Never use {% post_url %} tags.
9) Final response: a concise report — cycle number, issue number, verdict (published slug+commit / pending with due date / skipped with reason), what was researched, and the next engine fire expectation. This report is delivered to the user.
